Rosner Test

Source: R/stats.R
rosner_test.Rd

Performs Rosner's test for one or more potential outliers in environmental monitoring data.

rosner_test(df, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
rosner_test(
  df,
  location_id = "location_id",
  param_name = "param_name",
  sample_date = "sample_date",
  analysis_result = "analysis_result",
  default_unit = "default_unit",
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'env_schema'
rosner_test(df, k = 3, alpha = 0.05, warn = TRUE, keep_data_object = FALSE)

Arguments

df

A data frame or `env_schema` object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

location_id

Location column name.

param_name

Analyte column name.

sample_date

Sample date column.

analysis_result

Analytical result column name.

default_unit

Reporting unit column name.

k

Maximum number of candidate outliers evaluated.

alpha

Significance level.

warn

Logical indicating whether Rosner test warnings should be returned.

keep_data_object

Logical indicating whether the complete Rosner result object should be retained.

Value

A tibble containing one row per outlier evaluation group.

Details

`rosner_test()` is an S3 generic supporting both `data.frame` and `env_schema` objects.

If the input is grouped using [dplyr::group_by()], Rosner tests are performed within the existing groups.

Rosner's test evaluates multiple candidate outliers simultaneously and is commonly used in environmental and groundwater statistical evaluations.

When groups contain insufficient data, no outlier evaluation is performed and missing values are returned.

Groundwater Monitoring

Rosner's test is often preferred for groundwater monitoring datasets because it can evaluate multiple potential outliers and generally performs better than Dixon's or Grubbs' tests when sample sizes are sufficiently large.

env_schema Method

For `env_schema` objects, Rosner tests use standardized `.analysis_result` values.

Existing `dplyr::group_by()` groups are preserved. When the input is not grouped, tests are performed by:

  • location

  • analyte

  • analysis unit

#' @returns A tibble containing one row per outlier evaluation group.

The returned table includes:

Value

Observation evaluated by Rosner's procedure.

Outlier

Logical indicator identifying observations classified as outliers.

Examples

schema <- env_schema(
  gw_data,
  location = location_id,
  date = sample_date,
  analyte = param_name,
  result = analysis_result,
  unit = default_unit
)
#> Error in alias_lookup %>% dplyr::count(alias) %>% dplyr::filter(n > 1): could not find function "%>%"

rosner_test(schema)
#> Error: object 'schema' not found

schema |>
  dplyr::group_by(location_id) |>
  rosner_test()
#> Error: object 'schema' not found
